activities.title: Compass deflection near current-carrying wire
activities.summary: Pass current through a thick copper wire near a compass; the needle deflects — current produces a magnetic effect.

activities.title: Iron filings pattern around a bar magnet
activities.summary: Sprinkle iron filings near a bar magnet; they align along magnetic field lines.

activities.title: Drawing magnetic field lines with a compass
activities.summary: Move a small compass around a bar magnet and mark points to draw field lines.

activities.title: Direction of field around a straight conductor
activities.summary: Reverse current direction in a wire over a compass; deflection reverses — field direction follows current.

activities.title: Magnetic field pattern around straight conductor
activities.summary: Pass wire through cardboard with iron filings; concentric circles show field pattern.

activities.title: Field due to a circular coil
activities.summary: Iron filings around a current-carrying circular coil show field pattern; n turns multiply field strength.

activities.title: Force on a current-carrying rod in a magnetic field
activities.summary: Aluminium rod between magnet poles displaces when current flows; direction reverses with current or field.

exercise_mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the magnetic field near a long straight wire?
options: The field consists of straight lines perpendicular to the wire.
The field consists of straight lines parallel to the wire.
The field consists of radial lines originating from the wire.
The field consists of concentric circles centred on the wire.
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying wire form concentric circles in a plane perpendicular to the wire.

exercise_mcqs.question: At the time of short circuit, the current in the circuit
exercise_mcqs.explanation: A short circuit offers very low resistance, so current increases dangerously.

intext_samples.question: The field at the centre of a long circular coil carrying current will be parallel straight lines.
intext_samples.explanation: Inside a long solenoid/circular coil the field lines are parallel straight lines.

intext_samples.question: A wire with a green insulation is usually the live wire of an electric supply.
intext_samples.explanation: Live wire is red, neutral is black, earth wire is green.

intext_samples.question: Magnetic field lines around a bar magnet
options: cross each other at the poles
emerge from N and merge at S outside the magnet
start and end at infinity only
intext_samples.explanation: Field lines emerge from north pole and enter south pole outside the magnet; they form closed curves.

intext_samples.question: In domestic circuits, appliances are connected in parallel so that
options: same current flows through each appliance
each appliance gets the same potential difference and works independently
only one appliance can work at a time
intext_samples.explanation: Parallel connection gives 220 V across each branch and independent operation.
